Lexi Conquest: Dutch (Netherlands), 3–11-letter selection

Derived lexical data and frequency-based selections: CC BY-SA 4.0.
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
Full license: CC-BY-SA-4.0.txt in this directory. Game code has its separate license.

Lexical data: English Wiktionary contributors, Dutch entries, extracted by
Wiktextract and distributed by Kaikki. The answer selection targets contemporary Netherlands Dutch.
Broad dictionary guesses can include labelled regional or historical forms.
Source: https://kaikki.org/dictionary/Dutch/kaikki.org-dictionary-Dutch.jsonl
Source index and rights: https://kaikki.org/dictionary/
Source entry links: https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/<original-headword>#Dutch
Reuse terms: https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Terms_of_Use#7._Licensing_of_Content

The pinned input is Kaikki's postprocessed per-language snapshot, deprecated
upstream, not the raw multilingual Wiktextract extract. Imported 2026-11-06.
SHA-256: 6e3335a4bcf9739cae0a7490beb1f31d8e8dcec61475fc701a6cfe63cdd65438
No exact per-entry article revision is supplied. Per-record input hashes and
original spellings are retained in the repository. Credit: Tatu Ylonen,
Wiktextract: Wiktionary as Machine-Readable Structured Data, LREC 2022,
pp. 1317-1325, https://www.lrec-conf.org/proceedings/lrec2022/pdf/2022.lrec-1.140.pdf

Changes: retain lowercase 3–11-letter lexical headwords, parts of speech,
selected English glosses, usage labels and form/alternative relationships.
Exclude enrichment categories/disambiguation, audio, media, quotations,
examples, etymology, translations and non-Latin spellings. Preserve accents and trema using NFC and uppercase for play. IJ occupies
two tiles, including Unicode Ĳ/ĳ normalized to IJ. Y is never mapped to IJ. Original source spellings remain in definition attribution. A broad
attested-guess list and conservative common-answer subset are separate. Source
usage labels and editorial exclusions filter answers, not every displayed sense.
At most eight entries and eight senses per entry are displayed per spelling.

Frequency metadata: wordfreq v3.0.2, Robyn Speer and contributors, revision
372f6dbb3bd2ad4b675a3b18b94d44d0dd5fea8b, small_nl.msgpack.gz.
https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq/tree/372f6dbb3bd2ad4b675a3b18b94d44d0dd5fea8b
SHA-256: ae0d64f10e9d11898b2b9481c0b20698ec40c79b8025edfdd70856bd593ad4b0
Data: CC BY-SA 4.0. Version 3.0.2 software: MIT. Complete pinned README and
MIT notice are supplied in this directory. Preserve all README source credits,
including OpenSubtitles and freely available SUBTLEX, Marc Brysbaert and
coauthors. No corpus sentences are distributed. Retained spelling estimates
are historical, not current sense-specific or regional frequency measurements.
For case/IJ-ligature merged spellings, use the maximum estimate, not a sum.

No native-human review or exhaustive Dutch dictionary coverage is claimed.
Source extraction, labels and model editorial review can contain errors.
Dictionary glosses are not full
lessons or usage guarantees. Authored example sentences are not included.
Meaning availability never determines whether a word is accepted as a guess.
No words are automatically sent to an external service by the game.

Sources, checksums, policy and offline reproduction are documented in
WORDS-LICENSE.md and src/data/dutch/source.json in the source repository:
https://github.com/intrepion/kata-inspired-by-wordle-codex-dot
Preserve attribution, modification notices and CC BY-SA 4.0 ShareAlike terms
when redistributing adapted data. These notices add no extra restrictions.
